sentences.text: Order On Board 08/05/2024 1.

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V.Act') has been filed against award dated 06/12/2018 passed by the 1 st Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Smt. Basanti Rajwade vs Chandrakant Jha on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115743280/

Smt. Basanti Rajwade vs Chandrakant Jha on
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 Ambikapur, District - Surguja (CG) in Central Filing No.94/2018.

2. By the impugned award, learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,95,000/- in favour of the claimants as compensation on account of death of Anjali Rajwade in an unfortunate accident that took place on 26/08/2017 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle (Bolero Pick-up) bearing Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16767 registration No.UP 64 H 8669 driven and owned by respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.2 / insurance company.
The claimants are parents of the deceased.

3. As per claim application, the deceased Anjali Rajwade was aged about 11 years and she would have definitely succeeded in her life and after growing up, she would have contributed to the livelihood of her parents/claimants.
Therefore, Rs.2,95,000/- was claimed.
Respondent No.1 resisted the claim application.

Respondent No.2/ insurer of the offending vehicle in the written statement pleaded that the offending vehicle was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and respondent No.1 was not holding valid and effective driving license.
4. Learned Tribunal after framing issues, decided those issues in favour of the appellants / claimants and awarded compensation as stated above.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants / claimants submits that the law with regard to death of a child is no longer res integra in view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kishan Gopal and anr. v. Lala and ors., (2014) 1 SCC 244 and Kurvan Ansari @ Kurvan Ali and anr. v.
Shyam Kishore Murmu and anr., (2022) 1 SCC 317.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and anr. v. Lala and ors., (2014) 1 SCC 244
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:

Shyam Kishore Murmu and anr., (2022) 1 SCC 317
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that the amount of compensation on other heads is also on the lower side.

6. Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 supports the award passed by the learned Tribunal and submits that looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, just compensation has been awarded.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the records.

8. In the light of judgments passed in the case of Kurvan Ansari (supra) and Kishan Gopal (supra),
this Court feels that ends of justice would be served by awarding Rs.5 lakhs to the appellants /
claimants.

9. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed and amount of Rs.5 lakhs is awarded to the appellants /
claimants.
After deducting Rs.2,95,000/- as awarded by learned Tribunal, enhancement comes to Rs.2,05,000/-.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16767 Respondent No.2/insurance company shall pay the amount of Rs.2,05,000/- within a period of 60 days with 6% interest from the date of claim application.

After the amount of compensation is deposited by respondent No.2/insurance company, learned Tribunal Smt. Basanti Rajwade vs Chandrakant Jha on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115743280/
2 shall pass appropriate order for apportionment, investment and disbursement.
